rules: Keeping the same fundamental leg (e.g. $asset_turnover, $roe) while only swapping the price/volume-side term isn't enough to decorrelate: CS_RANK($asset_turnover)*COUNT(...) hit rho 0.847 vs an archived CS_RANK($asset_turnover)*CS_ZSCORE term, and CS_RANK($roe)*(ratio/TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63)) shared 5 nodes with an archived CS_RANK($roe) member despite a different window/structure. Vary the fundamental leg or its wrapper too, not just the other side.

($high-$low)/($close+eps), ($close-$high)/($close+eps) and ($close-$low)/($close+eps) -- raw, TS_RANK-wrapped, or divided by TS_MAX($high,21) -- are already claimed leaves on their own. Wrapping RANK/CS_RANK($earnings_per_share) around any of them, by subtraction or multiplication, still tripped archive_subtree at 5-7 shared nodes 4 times this round. Change the price-ratio leaf itself, not the eps wrapper.

In TS_CORR($high-$low, ..., 21) the volume-side term needs to be a change, not a level: TS_DELTA($dollar_volume,5) there scored 5.161, but DELAY($dollar_volume,1) in the same slot failed cheap_screen at |t| 0.14. Use deltas, not levels/lags, as the volume-side correlation input.

COUNT(CS_RANK($dollar_volume)>0.9,21) accepted at 3.520, but COUNT($dollar_volume>TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,10),21) duplicated the $volume analog at rho 0.915. For dollar_volume COUNT features, use a cross-sectional rank threshold, not a trailing-self-mean threshold.

CS_RANK($operating_margin)/(CS_RANK($dollar_volume)+eps) scored |t| 0.99, essentially at the cheap-screen edge. Worth retrying with a different fundamental numerator or a light transform before dropping the shape.

($close-TS_MIN($low,w))/(TS_MAX($high,w)-TS_MIN($low,w)+eps) is saturated across window changes alone: w=42 hit rho 0.950 against the w=21 version. This stochastic-style chassis needs a structural change, not just a new window.

The round's best fitness (7.873) came from RANK($earnings_per_share) times a downside-distance-from-high term, ($low-TS_MAX($high,21))/($close+eps), rather than a close- or high-anchored ratio -- those collided with the archive instead. The low-vs-recent-high anchor is the more productive eps partner right now.

The TS_MEAN(($close-$low)/(X+eps),10) sweep over denominator field X produced 2 of the round's 3 within-run duplicate rejects (X=TS_STD($close,126) and X=LOG($dollar_volume) each resubmitted). Dedupe candidate X's before submitting a sweep like this.
